rationale: C10 plausibly supplied a material template because both directives assign the Civil Service Commission responsibility for administering federal reemployment rights and expressly empower it to issue implementing regulations or procedures. The child adapts that same administrative machinery from expiring and administering specified executive-order-based rights to determining the applicability of statutory reemployment provisions for former federal employees who served in the armed forces or merchant marine. C25 has similar Commission rulemaking machinery and a reemployment subject, but concerns Foreign Service reinstatement and is less directly parallel. C01 merely adjusts one employee's reemployment eligibility and lacks the Commission-centered administrative structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Commission shall also determine the applicability, in general and in specific cases, of the reemployment provisions
shared_material.parent_excerpt: All existing reemployment rights to positions in the Federal service acquired under authority of [specified directives] ... shall expire
shared_material.explanation: Both provisions address the administration and scope of federal-service reemployment rights, though the child substitutes statutory military and merchant-marine rights for the earlier directive-based rights.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Commission may issue such regulations or instructions as it may deem necessary or appropriate for carrying out the said reemployment provisions
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Civil Service Commission is authorized to prescribe such rules and regulations and to establish such procedures as may be necessary for the administration of this order.
shared_material.explanation: This is a close substantive and linguistic parallel: each grants the Civil Service Commission implementing rulemaking and procedural authority for reemployment provisions.
